context_of_use: Simple synthetic engineering evidence for R-peak detection and RR measurement across independent rate and acquisition-stress cases.
evidence_boundary: Synthetic engineering QA evidence for R-peak detection and beat-to-beat RR measurement; not diagnosis, clinical validation, or regulatory qualification.

evidence_profile.description: A permissive engineering gate for baseline implementations. It is not a clinical, regulatory, or algorithm-class claim.
evidence_profile.threshold_adjustment: Relative to Level 2: minimum gates are reduced by 0.10 (floor 0); maximum error gates are multiplied by 1.25.

truth_policy.artifact_overlap: Noise and artifacts remain scoreable because each complete case is the unit of evaluation.
truth_policy.boundary: Only construction events crossing the record boundary are excluded; no blanket edge window is used.
truth_policy.event_reporting_basis: R-peak TP, FP, FN, sensitivity and positive predictive value use a 150 ms closest-event window, comparable to the default WFDB bxb reporting convention. Synsigra does not claim bxb identity or EC57 conformity.
truth_policy.event_scoreability: Complete in-record constructed QRS events are scoreable; every exclusion is reported.
truth_policy.literature_context: Thresholds are pre-specified for this exact deterministic synthetic protocol, informed by PhysioNet MIT-BIH Noise Stress Test Database and peer-reviewed noisy-QRS benchmarks; SNR labels are not directly interchangeable across protocols.
truth_policy.rr_association: Valid RR intervals are anchored by their ending R-peak time and associated when their overlap covers more than half of the shorter interval. FP splits and FN merges create local comparison pairs; unique interval coverage cannot exceed 100%.
truth_policy.rr_definition: Difference between consecutive scoreable construction R-peak times; the first beat has no in-record RR value.
truth_policy.rr_statistics_boundary: RR tolerance percentage, MAE and median are pre-specified case gates. P95 remains a visible diagnostic because split/merge outliers make it unsuitable as the primary ladder gate. These are Synsigra engineering limits, not ANSI/AAMI EC57 or IEC conformity claims.
truth_policy.scope: R-peak event and RR measurement files are required; no signal-quality output or claim is requested.
